key_results: Half-life of 229mTh+ determined to be 0.46(8) s; differs by orders of magnitude from neutral isomer, indirectly suggesting electronic bridge decay
comments: Result strongly implies existence of previously unconfirmed higher-order decay process; important for thorium-based nuclear clock development.

model_io.model: 229mTh+ ion in trap via charge-exchange reaction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Electronic bridge decay occurs in 229mTh+ at higher rate than internal conversion
hypotheses.result: Half-life difference indirectly suggests bridge decay channel exists

title: Capillary Leidenfrost effect
task: Demonstrating capillary Leidenfrost effect for stable, sustained levitation below conventional Leidenfrost point
key_results: Capillary structure enables levitation at temperatures below droplet Leidenfrost point; sustained self-propulsion and load delivery demonstrated on practical scale; effect is generic across natural materials and metals; no specialized surface treatment required
comments: Clever use of capillary geometry to stabilize liquid interface; practical temperature reduction and accessibility make this promising for contactless transport applications.

model_io.model: Periodically-arranged capillary structure with evaporating liquid

hypotheses.hypothesis: Capillary geometry reduces levitation onset temperature below Leidenfrost point
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; sustained levitation and transport achieved without special surfaces

title: Detection of atmospheric 42Ar at the 10−21 level by atom counting
task: Detection of rare atmospheric isotope 42Ar at isotopic abundance 10−21
key_results: Direct detection of 42Ar at 10−21 abundance using atom trap trace analysis; detection limit several orders of magnitude beyond existing methods on 10 L sample
comments: Elimination of isobar interference via atom counting is elegant; implications for argon-dating and dark-matter detector backgrounds are significant.

model_io.model: Atom trap trace analysis with isotope pre-enrichment

hypotheses.hypothesis: Laser-based atom counting eliminates isobar interference limits
hypotheses.result: Achieved 10−21 abundance detection, far exceeding accelerator mass spectrometry

title: Simultaneous Pi2 pulsation detected by CSES-01, Swarm, RBSP and Arase satellites
task: Multi-satellite detection and analysis of Pi2 magnetic pulsations across ionosphere-magnetosphere
key_results: Pi2 event (12:40–12:56 UT, Jan 12, 2019) observed simultaneously by CSES-01, Swarm, RBSP, Arase; high-frequency (m ~−1.7) and low-frequency (|m|~0.3) components; duskside cavity resonance characteristics identified
comments: Unique multi-mission coordination reveals waveguide and cavity modes; penetration speeds exceed average Alfvén speed, supporting sunward propagation.

model_io.model: Magnetosphere-ionosphere system during Pi2 pulsation event
inputs: CSES-01, Swarm A/C, RBSP A/B, Arase satellite magnetic field data

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-frequency Pi2 propagates via waveguide; low-frequency exhibits cavity resonance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; duskside signatures show cavity behavior; propagation speeds support distinct mechanisms

title: First-principles study of hydrogen-related defects at the a-SiO2/Si(100) interface
task: First-principles study of hydrogen-related defects at amorphous SiO2/Si interface with electrostatic corrections
key_results: Electrostatic corrections shift charge transition levels by up to 0.44 eV; formation energies span 1.71–5.23 eV; spatial position within suboxide layer controls thermodynamic stability
comments: Inclusion of electrostatic corrections via Poisson–DFT coupling is rigorous; results clarify interfacial defect behavior critical for device reliability.

model_io.model: Amorphous SiO2/Si(100) interface with hydrogen-related defects (DFT + Poisson)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Electrostatic corrections are essential for accurate charge transition levels at buried interfaces
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; corrections cause substantial shifts, enabling reliable defect characterization

title: Moiré artifact reduction in grating interferometry using multiple harmonics and total variation regularization
task: Reducing Moiré artifacts in X-ray grating interferometry via multi-harmonic analysis and total variation regularization
key_results: Algorithm recovers true phase-stepping positions; removes Moiré artifacts in attenuation, differential-phase, and dark-field images; validated on Talbot-Lau and Modulated Phase Grating Interferometers
comments: Practical image recovery approach using standard regularization; essential for X-ray interferometry clinical translation.

model_io.model: X-ray grating interferometer (Talbot-Lau, Modulated Phase Grating)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-harmonic analysis with TV regularization recovers true phase steps and eliminates Moiré
hypotheses.result: Confirmed on PMMA and biological samples

title: Unveiling enhanced HCN sensing: a comparative DFT study on reactivity and sensitivity of X-doped biphenylene nanotubes (X = B, Al, and Ga)
task: DFT assessment of doped biphenylene nanotubes for HCN gas sensing
key_results: B-, Al-, Ga-doped BPNTs show adsorption energies > −1 eV vs. −0.12 eV pristine; ~9% energy-gap reduction; short recovery times predicted; charge transfer primarily from HCN N lone pair and C−N π bond
comments: Rational design strategy via doping is sound; computational predictions need experimental validation for sensor viability.

model_io.model: Doped biphenylene nanotubes (DFT with B, Al, Ga dopants)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Doping creates active sites for strong, spontaneous HCN adsorption
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; doped systems show >8× stronger interaction and enhanced sensing characteristics

title: Implications of Pr3+ ions on structural, opto-thermal features of alkali zinc boro-tellurite glass systems for optical and laser technology applications
task: Characterizing Pr3+-doped borotellurite glasses for LED and laser optical applications
key_results: Thermal stability: Tg 409–461 °C, Tc 511–572 °C; emission at 488 nm (3P0→3H4) and 605 nm (3P1→3H5); orange CCT <4000 K (warm), blue >4000 K (cool); refractive index 2.356–2.368; energy gap 3.110–3.154 eV
comments: Comprehensive optical and thermal characterization; warm-and-cool CCT tunability attractive for RGB displays.

model_io.model: Pr3+-doped alkali zinc boro-tellurite glass (0–2 mol% Pr6O11)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pr3+ doping tunes luminescence and optical properties for LED/laser use
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; warm and cool CCT ranges achieved with good thermal stability

title: Quantitative model for imaging single fiber reflectance spectroscopy
task: Quantitative modeling of imaging single-fiber reflectance (iSFR) spectroscopy for tissue optics retrieval
key_results: iSFR model predicts reflectance with 6.2% median error vs. Monte Carlo; inverse retrieval of absorption/scattering within ~10% over broad noise range; distance-based probability weighting reduces computational cost
comments: Efficient surrogate approach for probe design; contact-free geometry addresses artifacts of conventional single-fiber methods.

model_io.model: Monte Carlo-based iSFR model with distance-weighted reflectance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Distance-based weighting replaces explicit source-detector simulation while maintaining accuracy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; enables efficient forward and inverse spectroscopy models

title: Tunable field-linked s-wave interactions in dipolar fermi mixtures
task: Tuning s-wave interactions in dipolar fermionic mixtures using microwave fields
key_results: Universal s-wave resonance accessible without compromising microwave shielding; universal description of tunable interaction developed from field parameters
comments: Removes experimental constraint that previously existed with p-wave interactions, opening practical routes to strongly-interacting dipolar spin mixtures.

model_io.model: Fermionic dipolar spin mixture (microwave-shielded molecules)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Universal s-wave resonance is accessible without compromising shielding
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; enables stable, tunable interaction in dipolar fermion mixtures

title: Attaining physics-driven convolutional operators by architecture design
task: Developing physics-driven convolutional operator for multiscale predictive modeling without labeled data
key_results: Operator trained entirely on physics constraints (no high-fidelity data); median error 6.2% on reflectance prediction; outperforms prior operator learners on micromechanics, elastic waves, and microstructure evolution
comments: Knowledge-based training addresses critical bottleneck of expensive simulations; generalization across PDE families is notable.

model_io.model: Physics-driven recurrent convolutional neural network
outputs: PDE solutions (micromechanics, wave propagation, microstructure evolution)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Purely physics-constrained training produces robust surrogate operators
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; labeled-data-free approach outperforms data-driven methods
